extracted.intended_audience: lawgivers, legislators, and statesmen designing constitutions; students of political philosophy
extracted.subtask_description: Practical and normative guidance for establishing and preserving different forms of government (democracy, oligarchy, magistracies) in a polis; advice aimed at those who would found, correct, or maintain a state. Covers institutional design, selection and duties of magistrates, fiscal rules, military composition, and social/legal measures to secure stability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foundation of a democratically constituted state
rubrics_metrics.description: Now the foundation of a democratical state is liberty, and people have been accustomed to say this as if here only liberty was to be found; for they affirm that this is the end proposed by every democracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Liberty is the organizing principle: political equality and freedom of living as one pleases are treated as democratic ends. Use this as the normative starting-point when designing democratic institutions; beware that 'liberty' here includes rotation of power and popular rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Democratic justice: equality measured by numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: According to democratical justice, equality is measured by numbers, and not by worth: and this being just, it is necessary that the supreme power should be vested in the people at large; and that what the majority determine should be final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design decisions, offices, and powers so that the majority (numerical equality) governs; expect this to privilege poorer/more numerous classes. Use majority rule as a defining criterion; consider tensions with property-based claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rotation, lot selection, and limits on office in democracies
rubrics_metrics.description: All the magistrates should be chosen out of all the people, and all to command each, and each in his turn all: that all the magistrates should be chosen by lot, except to those offices only which required some particular knowledge and skill: that no census, or a very small one, should be required... that none should be in the same employment twice, or very few, and very seldom, except in the army: that all their appointments should be limited to a very short time...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor broad recruitment from the citizenry, extensive use of sortition, very short terms, and restrictions on reappointment to prevent oligarchic accumulation. Exempt specialized or technical offices from lotting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial inclusiveness and limits on magistrates' discretion
rubrics_metrics.description: That the whole community should be qualified to judge in all causes whatsoever... that the supreme power should be in the public assembly; and that no magistrate should be allowed any discretionary power but in a few instances, and of no consequence to public business.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maximize popular participation in adjudication and collective decision-making; tightly limit discretionary powers of magistrates to prevent abuses and ensure assembly oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Paying citizens for public roles
rubrics_metrics.description: There should, if possible, be a fund to pay all the citizens--who have any share in the management of public affairs, either as members of the assembly, judges, and magistrates; but if this cannot be done, at least the magistrates, the judges the senators, and members of the supreme assembly, and also those officers who are obliged to eat at a common table ought to be paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide public pay to enable broad civic participation; if resources limited, prioritize payment for magistrates, judges, senators, and those otherwise economically burdened by civic service.

rubrics_metrics.name: No life-tenure offices in democracies
rubrics_metrics.description: In this state also no office should be for life; and, if any such should remain after the government has been long changed into a democracy, they should endeavour by degrees to diminish the power; and also elect by lot instead of vote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eliminate or curtail life offices when democratizing; replace permanent appointments with short, revocable terms and sortition to limit entrenched privilege.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure to procure fair equality between rich and poor
rubrics_metrics.description: Let that be established which is approved of by both these, or the greater part: but should there be opposite sentiments, let that be established which shall be approved of by the greater part: but let this be according to the census... and should these happen to be equal, it should be regarded as a case similar to an assembly or court of justice dividing equally... determine it by lot or some such method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When designing representation, balance the interests of property-holders and the numerically larger poor by weighting votes or using combined mechanisms (census-weighting plus majority) and provide tie-breaking methods (lot, rotation) to resolve deadlocks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of democracies by social composition
rubrics_metrics.description: There are four kinds of democracies. The best is that which is composed of those first in order... this also is the most ancient of any. I call that the first which every one would place so, was he to divide the people; for the best part of these are the husbandmen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize that the socio-economic base (husbandmen, shepherds, mechanics, hired servants) affects the character and stability of a democracy; prefer agrarian-majority compositions when aiming for stability and moderation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Property and land regulations to stabilize democracy
rubrics_metrics.description: To establish a democracy of husbandmen some of those laws which were observed in many ancient states are universally useful; as, for instance, on no account to permit any one to possess more than a certain quantity of land, or within a certain distance from the city. Formerly also, in some states, no one was allowed to sell their original lot of land. They also mention a law of one Oxylus, which forbade any one to add to their patrimony by usury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement landholding caps, restrictions on sale of original lots, and limits on accumulation by usury to prevent extreme inequality that undermines democracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social and religious integration measures
rubrics_metrics.description: It is, moreover, very-useful in such a state to do as Clisthenes did at Athens... to institute many tribes and fraternities, and to make the religious rites of private persons few, and those common; and every means is to be contrived to associate and blend the people together as much as possible; and that all former customs be broken through.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use civic institutions, shared religious rites, tribes, and clubs to bind diverse citizenry, reduce factionalism, and foster unity; weakening exclusive private customs can help blend social groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of confiscatory incentives in courts
rubrics_metrics.description: They should therefore endeavour to procure its safety... avoiding what is hurtful... our demagogues at present, to flatter the people, occasion frequent confiscations in the courts; for which reason those who have the welfare of the state really at heart should act directly opposite to what they do, and enact a law to prevent forfeitures from being divided amongst the people or paid into the treasury, but to have them set apart for sacred uses.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prohibit rewarding litigants or courts with confiscated property to remove perverse incentives for prosecutions and corruption; set forfeitures aside for public/sacred purposes to reduce opportunistic prosecutions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restrict number/duration of assemblies and courts when revenues are small
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever, then, the revenues of the state are small, there should be but few public assemblies and but few courts of justice: these, however, should have very extensive jurisdictions, but should continue sitting a few days only...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When public coffers are limited, limit frequency and duration of assemblies and courts to reduce costs while preserving broad jurisdiction; prefer short sittings to attract wealthy participation and improve judgment quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use public funds to make majority prosperous rather than perpetual dole
rubrics_metrics.description: The true patriot in a democracy ought to take care that the majority of the community are not too poor... what can be saved out of the public money should be put by, and then divided at once amongst the poor, if possible, in such a quantity as may enable every one of them to purchase a little field... or at least to give each of them enough to procure the implements of trade and husbandry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer one-time investments that enable self-sufficiency (land, tools) over recurring handouts; aim to raise the baseline prosperity of the majority to reduce social instability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mixed selection methods for magistracies (lot and vote)
rubrics_metrics.description: They have also two different ways of electing their magistrates; for some are chosen by vote, others by lot; by the last, that the people at large may have some share in the administration; by the former, that the state may be well governed: the same may be accomplished if of the same magistrates you choose some by vote, others by lot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combine sortition and election to balance broad participation with competence: allocate routine/administrative posts by lot and critical/technical posts by vote or merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oligarchy foundation: dual census and rule by better sort
rubrics_metrics.description: The first and best-framed oligarchy is that which approaches near to what we call a free state; in which there ought to be two different census, the one high, the other low: from those who are within the latter the ordinary officers of the state ought to be chosen; from the former the supreme magistrates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design oligarchies with graded censuses to distinguish ordinary officeholders from supreme magistrates; ensure commonalty within the included census retain some superiority over excluded masses to avoid revolt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Oligarchical practice of public benefaction to secure favor
rubrics_metrics.description: It is necessary that the magistrates, upon entering into their offices, should make magnificent sacrifices and erect some public structure, that the people partaking of the entertainment, and seeing the city ornamented with votive gifts in their temples and public structures, may see with pleasure the stability of the government: add to this also, that the nobles will have their generosity recorded...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage elites to perform conspicuous public benefactions (sacrifices, monuments, entertainments) to legitimize oligarchic rule and secure popular goodwill; avoid obvious accumulation-of-gain motives which breed resentment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Military composition shapes constitutional form
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the nature of the country can admit a great number of horse; there a powerful oligarchy may be easily established: for the safety of the inhabitants depends upon a force of that sort... the light-armed and the sailors always contribute to support a democracy...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Account for dominant military types when designing regime: cavalry/heavy-arm tends to empower wealthier classes (oligarchy); light-armed/sailor forces empower broader citizenry (democracy). Balanced military composition mitigates factional advantage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid arming demographic groups that undermine ruling class
rubrics_metrics.description: For it is with those that the populace get the better of the men of fortune in an insurrection; for these being lighter are easily a match for the horse and the heavy-armed: so that for an oligarchy to form a body of troops from these is to form it against itself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If preserving oligarchic rule, avoid relying primarily on light-armed or sailor levies who can be instruments of popular insurrection; mix troop types to reduce internal vulnerability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Magistracy sizing and separation according to city size and function
rubrics_metrics.description: It is necessary that in small states the magistrates should be few; in a large one, many: also to know well what offices may be joined together, and what ought to be separated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scale the number of magistrates with polity size and clearly delineate which roles can be combined and which must be distinct to prevent conflict of interest and centralization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core civic administrative offices and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The different departments of all those magistrates who are necessary: these are either religion, war, taxes, expenditures, markets, public buildings, harbours, highways. Belonging to the courts of justice there are scribes to enroll private contracts; and there must also be guards set over the prisoners, others to see the law is executed, council on either side, and also others to watch over the conduct of those who are to decide the causes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure explicit offices for markets, public works, harbors, highways, revenue collection, record-keeping, prisons/execution, legal oversight, and religious caretaking. Allocate responsibilities to specialized magistrates to secure administration and order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financial officers: receivers/quaestors and auditors
rubrics_metrics.description: There must also be other officers appointed to receive the public revenue and to deliver it out to those who are in the different departments of the state: these are called receivers or quaestors... Since some of the magistrates, if not all, have business with the public money, it is necessary that there should be other officers, whose employment should be nothing else than to take an account of what they have, and correct any mismanagement therein.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create separate revenue-receiving and disbursing roles, and independent auditors/accountants to monitor public funds and correct mismanagement. Separation reduces embezzlement and increases fiscal transparency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registers/notaries to enroll contracts and proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: There must also be another, before whom all private contracts and sentences of courts should be enrolled, as well as proceedings and declarations. Sometimes this employment is divided amongst many, but there is one supreme over the rest; these are called proctors, notaries, and the like.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain centralized, authoritative public records of contracts and judgments administered by notaries/proctors to ensure legal certainty and continuity; consider hierarchical organization of record offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of sentencing and execution to avoid odium
rubrics_metrics.description: It is best that this office should not be executed by one person, but by some of the magistrates of the other courts... by so much the less odium attends those who carry the laws into execution, by so much the easier will they be properly put in force: therefore for the same persons to pass the sentence and to execute it will subject them to general hatred.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Separate the roles of judges (who pass sentence) and executioners/administrators (who carry sentences into effect) to spread odium and prevent concentration of coercive power; rotate odious duties among citizens to avoid permanent stigma.

rubrics_metrics.name: Execution office rotation and youth assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: This, therefore, ought by no means to be a separate office from others; nor should it be continually allotted to any individuals, but the young men; where there is a city-guard, the youths ought in turns to take these offices upon them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid making execution/enforcement a permanent career; allocate enforcement duties by rotation, often to younger citizens or guards, to prevent corruption and resistance to duty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supreme magistrate or council to preside and summon the people
rubrics_metrics.description: Since some of the magistrates... there is one who is supreme over them all, who very often has in his own power the disposal of the public revenue and taxes; who presides over the people when the supreme power is in them; for there must be some magistrate who has a power to summon them together, and to preside as head of the state. These are sometimes called preadvisers; but where there are many, more properly a council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designate a presiding magistrate or council with formal powers to convene assemblies, manage public finances, and coordinate magistracies; choose an institutional form (single magistrate vs council) suited to regime type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partition of magistracies by domain and specialized public roles
rubrics_metrics.description: To enumerate in few words the different departments of all those magistrates who are necessary: these are either religion, war, taxes, expenditures, markets, public buildings, harbours, highways... governors of the women; who are to see the laws are executed; who take care of the boys and preside over their education... those who have the care of their gymnastic exercises, their theatres, and every other public spectacle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider creating domain-specific magistracies (religious caretakers, education, women's governance where applicable, cultural/public spectacles) in polities with leisure and resources; tailor office structure to local needs and capacities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legislator's aim: stability over perfection
rubrics_metrics.description: It is also the business of the legislator and all those who would support a government of this sort not to make it too great a work, or too perfect; but to aim only to render it stable... and by framing such laws, written and unwritten, as contain those things which chiefly tend to the preservation of the state; nor to suppose that that is useful either for a democratic or an oligarchic form of government which contributes to make them more purely so, but what will contribute to their duration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize durability and pragmatic arrangements over idealized perfection. Enact written and customary laws that reduce causes of decay and avoid reforms that make a regime purer but more fragile.
